title: Adversarial Multiplicity: Cherry-Picked Models and the Limits of Disclosure
abstract: arXiv:2611.07378v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Predictive multiplicity -- where similarly accurate models disagree on individual predictions -- can be leveraged to optimize secondary metrics (e.g., fairness) without loss in predictive performance. However, exploiting multiplicity opens the opportunity for motivated parties (or coding agents gaming their objectives) to steer predictions toward their own ends, such as in litigation or consumer disputes with automated decision-making tools. In these adversarial multiplicity settings, we distinguish soft manipulation, where parties optimize over innocuous model choices (e.g., hyperparameter tuning, feature engineering), from hard manipulation, where parties directly perturb model parameters. We find a sufficiently flexible model can be manipulated to reverse any individual prediction with minimal change in predictive performance while passing black-box audits, making hard manipulation viable in most regulatory settings. Soft manipulation

translated_title: 对抗性多重性：精心挑选的模型与信息披露的局限
translated_abstract: 预测多重性——即准确度相近的模型在个体预测上可能产生分歧——可以被用来在保持预测性能的前提下优化次要指标（例如公平性）。然而，对多重性的利用为有动机的一方（或通过投机取巧来达成目标的编程智能体）提供了将预测导向自身目的的机会，例如在涉及自动化决策工具的诉讼或消费者纠纷中。在这些对抗性多重性场景中，我们区分了软性操纵与硬性操纵：前者指各方在无害的模型选择范围内进行优化（例如超参数调优、特征工程），后者指各方直接扰动模型参数。我们发现，一个足够灵活的模型可以被操纵，在预测性能变化极小的情况下逆转任何个体预测，并能通过黑盒审计，这使得硬性操纵在大多数监管环境中成为可行的手段。软性操纵……
tldr: 本文揭示了预测多重性可被恶意武器化——操纵者仅需微调模型（甚至在通过黑盒审计的情况下）就能在几乎不损失预测精度的前提下逆转任何个体预测结果，这从根本上挑战了基于信息披露的监管保障机制。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that predictive multiplicity can be adversarially weaponized: motivated parties can reverse any individual prediction with negligible accuracy loss—either through benign model selection or direct parameter perturbation—while passing black-box audits, fundamentally undermining disclosure-based regulatory safeguards.
